2607.29624.title: The Theoretical Foundation of Socratic Tests: Dynamic, Multimodal, Conversational Examinations
2607.29624.paper_summary: Traditional static assessments rely on a subtractive, deficit-based grading model that often penalizes ambition and obscures diagnostic feedback. Conversely, traditional face-to-face oral examinations introduce severe construct-irrelevant variance by exacerbating performative anxiety and the sociological power imbalances inherent to academic hierarchies. This paper presents the theoretical foundation for the "Socratic Test," an automated, computer-mediated conversational assessment. By integrating Dynamic Assessment principles, multimodal workspaces, Bloom's Taxonomy for real-time proctoring, and the SOLO Taxonomy for structural evaluation, the Socratic Test actively maps a student's cognitive boundaries. This paper formalizes the use of graduated scaffolding to quantify the Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD) and details a non-compensatory, additive grading architecture that prioritizes mastery over penalty and human-AI alignment to ensure unprecedented measurement reliability.
2607.29624.paper_summary_zh: 傳統的靜態評估依賴於一種減法的、基於缺陷的評分模型，這種模型常常懲罰雄心壯志並模糊診斷反饋。<lb/>相反，傳統的面對面口試則因加劇表現焦慮和學術階層固有的社會權力不平衡而引入了嚴重的構念無關變異。<lb/>本文提出了「蘇格拉底測試」的理論基礎，這是一種自動化的、計算機媒介的對話評估。<lb/>通過整合動態評估原則、多模態工作空間、布魯姆分類法進行實時監考，以及SOLO分類法進行結構評估，蘇格拉底測試積極地映射學生的認知邊界。<lb/>本文正式化了漸進式支架的使用，以量化最近發展區（ZPD），並詳細說明了一種非補償性、加法的評分架構，該架構優先考慮掌握而非懲罰，並在人類與人工智慧之間達成一致，以確保前所未有的測量可靠性。
2607.29624.author: Ilya Mikhelson et.al.
